notes: Security questionnaires, drafted from what Amphora actually does · Every import takes Excel, and gives back the rows to fix

entries.title: Security questionnaires, drafted from what Amphora actually does
items: Settings → Security questionnaires (owners and admins): choose a client's security questionnaire as Excel or CSV, and Amphora drafts an answer to every question from its security facts — what the software does, checked against its code, and how this install is set up right now (two-factor rule, session limits, password rules, backups and off-site copies, restore drills, SIEM forwarding, the AI assistant).

Questions about your company rather than the software — policies, people, insurance, offices, hosting provider, certifications — are never guessed: they come back Needs an answer for you to write. Every answer shows the facts it rests on, and you can edit any of them before downloading the client's file with the answers added.
Needs the AI assistant with the new Security questionnaire answers switch on; only the questions and the facts are sent, never your data.
Settings → Security now says two-factor “Required for owners, admins and managers” — managers were always included; the label left them out.

entries.title: Every import takes Excel, and gives back the rows to fix
items: Choose an Excel workbook (.xlsx) anywhere you could choose a CSV — SKU import, mass receiving, the move sheet, locations, portal rosters, SKU code changes, tracking numbers, the catalog layout, the carrier tools' bulk lists and a portal's bulk checkout. Before, an Excel file on the SKU import was read as gibberish and refused with “The file has no "sku" column”.
Dates in Excel read as dates, and a long number like a 12-digit UPC keeps every digit. An older .xls or a Numbers file gets a plain “save it as .xlsx or CSV”.

Download the rows to fix: when rows have problems, one click gives an Excel file of just those rows as they were in your file, with an error column saying what's wrong on each. Fix it and upload it again — the error column is skipped. The guided Import window's download and a portal's address check now come as Excel too, with every cell kept as text so codes and ZIPs with leading zeros survive.
The SKU import's problem list is easier to scan: each row on its own line with its code, the reason underneath. A move sheet's problems now always name the line in your file.

entries.title: Oversized Excel files are refused before they use up memory
items: An .xlsx that unpacks to more than 64 MB for its sheet, or 100 MB in all, is refused as it's opened: “This spreadsheet unpacks to more than 64 MB — save it as CSV, or split it.” A small file built to swell used to take over a gigabyte of the server's memory and slow everyone on that server.
The 20,000-row limit now applies while the sheet is read, so a too-long sheet is refused in moments instead of after being read in full.

entries.title: A row pasted twice no longer imports twice
items: Every import now skips a row that repeats an earlier row exactly — every cell the same — and names it “Same as line N”. The check says how many at the top. Before, the same order line pasted 1,000 times became an order with 1,000 lines, and a mass-receiving sheet pasted twice booked the delivery twice.
When the repeats are real, tick “Rows that repeat exactly are meant” and check again: every row goes in. Rows that only share a SKU but differ in any cell are never flagged.
A roster import skips the same person pasted twice, and a SKU import names an exact repeat “Same as line N”.

entries.title: A failed label purchase never blocks the shipment, and it emails you
items: When a carrier says no (a refused API key, a bad address, its own error), nothing is held: the pack screen shows the carrier's message, and once it's fixed you buy again. Before, some refusals left the shipment saying an earlier purchase “hasn't answered yet”.

When a purchase gets no answer at all, the pack screen asks “Did a label get bought?”. Choose No label was bought — buy again, or It was bought — enter tracking, right there. Anyone who can ship can choose, and no second label is bought until someone does.

Every failed label purchase, and refused carrier credentials on any carrier call, now reaches your problem-alert email (Settings → Health). The alert names the client, the order, the carrier and what the carrier said, and says what to check: Settings → Integrations → Carrier accounts, sandbox or production keys, and for FedEx, the Ship API on the project.
Void works on a label the carrier has never heard of: it's cleared here, with a note saying so.

entries.title: Adding a product with shades always asks which shade
items: A product's shades now follow it into user groups limited to “Only these categories” — file the parent and every shade comes along. Before, the shades were filtered out, so the product page offered no choice and Add to cart put the parent itself in the cart.

A product that comes in options can never be added to a cart on its own; when none of its options are open to someone, the page says so. “N options” on a card counts only the ones that person can order.

entries.title: FedEx delivery estimates work
items: Estimated delivery with a FedEx account no longer fails with “An invalid or null CarrierCodeType was entered” — Amphora now asks both FedEx Express and FedEx Ground.

entries.title: Launch rosters: create people now, invite them on launch day
items: Portal users have an account status and an invitation status of their own. New people start Pending activation — no sign-in, no email — and on launch day you activate a group and send the welcome emails in one go.
Users shows Account (Pending activation, Active, Inactive) and Invite (Not sent, Queued, Sent with the date, Failed with the reason, Accepted) as separate columns.
Create user adds someone as Pending activation and emails nobody. Create & send invite is there for a one-off.
Search, filter by group, role, account and invite, sort any column, tick people or select everyone the filters show.

Activate, Deactivate, Send welcome emails and Resend invitations for the selection. Each asks first with the number of emails and who's skipped and why; Send welcome emails never goes to someone already sent one.
A pending person can't get in — not by password, single sign-on, an old invitation link or a session — and the sign-in page tells them plainly their account isn't active yet.
Roster import is safe by default: new people are pending and nobody is emailed. Choose Active or Send the invitation now when you mean it; the summary counts created, activated and emailed.
Settings → Users: adding a team member no longer emails them unless you tick the box. Send welcome email under Manage sends it later with a fresh temporary password.
Activations, deactivations and invitations each go in the audit log.
API: creating a portal user without a password no longer emails them — send invite: true for that. New bulk endpoint, and the import takes activation.

entries.title: Critical problems by text, after hours
items: Settings → Health → Text messages: add the on-call phones (a 10-digit number and the carrier, Verizon or T-Mobile) and critical problems are texted to them as well as emailed. Texts go out through your own outgoing email to the carrier's email-to-text address, so there's nothing new to sign up for. Send a test text checks every phone.

Every problem is now Critical or Warning. Critical means an order, pick, pack, label, stock change or payment that failed to save, or a background job or the ordering platform connection that failed or went down. Warnings, such as a page that crashed in a browser or the store preview, are emailed only.

A text is one short line with the client, what went wrong, the area and a reference. It never includes people's details or passwords. When a texted outage on the ordering platform ends, a 'working again' text follows.
Alert emails now say Critical or Warning, the area, the client and which install sent them.

The same problem texts at most once an hour, and no more than 10 texts go out in an hour. A problem that keeps happening says so ('Still happening'). These limits now survive a restart and are shared by every process.
Delivery depends on the carrier's gateway and isn't guaranteed, so the email always goes out too.

entries.title: Variants: add many at once, bulk upload, and a Variants import
items: A SKU's Variants tab has + Add variants: search the customer's SKUs by code, name or description, tick as many as you need (or Select all matching), and add them in one go with their option labels suggested. Ticks are kept when you search again or change page.
SKUs that can't join stay in the list, greyed, with the reason: already an option of another parent, or has options of its own.
If the SKU holds stock or is on open orders, the tab says so before you pick anything.

Bulk upload variants on the same tab: a two-column sheet (Child SKU, Dropdown Display Name), checked row by row before anything is saved. Fix problems in place or download the rows that were left out.
Setup → Import → Variants sets up many parents from one file (Parent SKU, Child SKU, Dropdown Display Name), with the same checks.

entries.title: SKU import says what's required, with a short template
items: Import CSV on a customer's SKUs tab now says plainly what a file needs: sku on every row, and name on rows that create a new SKU. Everything else is optional — delete columns you don't use, in any order.
Two templates: Basic (12 columns — the required two plus the ones most catalogs fill in) and Advanced (all 64). Show all 64 columns lists each one as Required or Optional with what goes in it.

Choosing a file checks it straight away and nothing changes until you press Import. The check counts new SKUs and updates, and lists lines with no sku, new SKUs without a name, repeated SKUs and columns it doesn't recognise.
Columns the import doesn't recognise are now ignored and listed instead of stopping the whole file. A sku repeated in the file is taken from its first row; the later rows are reported.

entries.title: Portals say Powered by your company, and the calendar asks what your company should know
items: Calendar events ask What should <your company> know? (e.g. What should Hatteras know?) instead of What the warehouse should know.

Client portals' footer and sign-in page now say Powered by <your company> instead of Powered by Amphora. Settings → Branding → Client portals say “Powered by …” sets the name; blank uses the company name. It's a setting, so it survives updates.

entries.title: Categories one level at a time, and drag to move them
items: The Categories card shows the top level first; click a category to see what's inside it. The path above the list (All categories › Balani › Fitness) and Back take you up, Find a category searches every level, and the card remembers where you were.

Drag the six-dot handle to reorder categories or move one anywhere: hold over a category to open it, over the path to climb out, and the page scrolls by itself near the edges — a deep category goes to a completely different parent in one drag. A line or highlight shows where it will land, loops and duplicate names are refused, and every drop saves straight away with Undo.
Reshape the tree, a SKU's Categories and a user group's Only these categories use the same navigator.

entries.title: The knowledge base PDF downloads quickly
items: Knowledge base → Full reference (PDF) is less than half the size (about 22 MB instead of 53 MB) with the same pages and pictures, and once it has been made it downloads straight away for everyone until the next update. Handbooks and single articles too.

entries.title: Portal tab icon, studio while signed in as someone, kit stock said plainly
items: Design studio → Your brand → Browser tab icon: upload a square icon for the browser tab. Without one, a square logo is used, or the brand's first letter on its colour — wide logos no longer get squeezed.
The studio preview updates live even when you also have a Sign in as session open on that portal, and says whose view you're seeing, with End that session.
Kit choices that are out of stock say Out of stock in the portal, not just greyed out.
Labels with a hint no longer push their box below the others in a row (calendar reminders, counts, receiving, bulk order edits).

entries.title: Print sizes in millimetres, and proofs that show the cut
items: Pick a print size from standard sizes — A6 to A1, Letter, Tabloid, business card, posters — or type it in inches or millimetres. Bleed has one-click 0.125 in and 3 mm.
Proofs show the cut line, the bleed that's trimmed off and the keep-text-inside line, for buyers' uploads, personalized items and the staff print job page.

entries.title: Office: fewer clicks on orders, invoices, approvals and imports
items: One Change order button on an order; Ship, Close short and Cancel confirm in a window that says exactly what happens to stock and fees.
Invoices → Drafts: tick several and Issue & send them at once, each with its own result.
Approvers can Approve or Reject straight from the email — no sign-in; links work once and last 7 days.
The portal's My orders has search and pages, with tracking numbers as links.
Import check: correct a bad cell right there and check again — no spreadsheet round-trip.

entries.title: Floor: scans that finish the job
items: Scan mode saves the line you finished when you scan the next item, and says why if it can't.
Picking: scans count up, scanning the next bin confirms the stop, and a bin isn't scanned twice in a row.
Counts: count by scanning units, and add something unexpected you find in the bin.
Receive and Move suggest where to put the item; a received pallet offers Put away now.
Packing: rates load by themselves, one Buy & print label button, box weights estimated from the products.

entries.title: The ordering platform you can trust: safe sends, alerts and previews
items: Customer → Ordering platform opens with Is it working? — last synced per stream, and what's failing in plain words. Problems (refused login, the ordering platform down, no orders polled for 30 minutes, stuck items) are emailed to your problem alert addresses.
Every send to the ordering platform goes out once — no double pushes from overlapping syncs, webhooks or double clicks.
Preview what the stock push or following the ordering platform's stock would change, per SKU, before switching it on; nothing is written.
Switching on saves a copy of the ordering platform's numbers first (download as CSV), and every send is kept in a send history.
Receiving only compares like with like, new parts become SKUs only for live clients, a failed shipment check asks a person instead of guessing, and held orders go through on their own once fixed.

entries.title: The ordering platform people you can see and choose, and no button on the portal's welcome if you'd rather
items: Design studio → Hero → Button says now says it plainly: leave it empty and the welcome has no button (like Shop the catalog) at all.
Customer → Ordering platform → People shows the people straight away — name, email, group, role, how they'll sign in — with tabs for already here, skipped, user groups and cost centres.
Don't skip them: tick a shared or inactive ordering platform login to bring it in anyway (inactive ones stay switched off), or type an email for someone without one.

entries.title: Bring a client's people in from the ordering platform
items: Customer → Ordering platform → People reads the client's ordering platform user groups, users and accounting units and brings them in: groups by name, people with their role, power buyer, group and title, and cost centres. Nothing is written to the ordering platform.

People arrive inactive with no email, so they keep ordering in the ordering platform; on moving day, Go live switches them all on and sends the invitations (single sign-on people just become active). Shared logins, people with no email and duplicates are skipped and listed.

entries.title: Problem alerts by email, clearer preview errors, portal pages behind nginx, and a tidier Users list
items: Test worlds show the address testers can actually reach — inside Docker the link no longer shows the container's own address. Test worlds → Your worlds → Not the right address? Change… sets it once (like 192.168.113.40) for every world.
Customer → Client portal → Users: a Status column (Active, Invited · not accepted, Inactive), and Manage opens a person's actions under their row instead of a line of buttons running off the side.

Portal pages and the design studio's preview no longer fail with 502 Bad Gateway behind a web server (nginx) on its default settings: the storefront's fonts are no longer all announced up front, which made its response headers too big for the server.

Problem alerts: add email addresses under Settings → Health and they hear about it when something breaks — a server error, a crashed page, or the web server refusing Amphora's answer — through your own email setup, at most once an hour per problem. Send a test alert to check.

Each alert is the actual issue, in two parts: in plain words — what went wrong (named plainly when Amphora knows it), who it happened to, which client and record, where, and what to do — then the technical detail for whoever fixes it: the exact error, the request, the error reference, the version and the trace.
The design studio explains a failed preview instead of showing a bare 502 page: which server answered, what usually fixes it, and Try again.

entries.title: The design file brings the category tree and its pictures too
items: Design studio → Design file now carries every category with its picture, description and order. Bringing it in on live puts each picture on the matching category and makes the categories live doesn't have yet — assign products to them there.

entries.title: Clients add their people through the API — invited, or inactive until switched on
items: A new Manage users permission on client API keys: the brand's own systems add people as invited (the invitation email goes now) or inactive (no email; switch them on later and the invitation goes then).
They can also change a person's role, group and status by name, and resend an invitation. The key must act as a brand admin, like the People page.

entries.title: Packaging on each client's own dieline, with their art per panel
items: In the designer, add the client's dieline (PDF or AI): the page takes its size, and it shows over the page so you can draw a box on each panel — Lid, Front, sides — for the client's art.

Clients upload art per panel, checked at that panel's size. Proofs show it against the dieline; the print file never has the lines on the art, and the print-ready PDF adds the dieline as its own page for the cutter.

entries.title: Clients put their own artwork in a box on the design — checked and placed
items: A box on a design set to They upload it now takes the client's artwork as PDF, AI, SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP — not just a picture. It's checked at the box's printed size: too low a resolution is refused with the reason, soft is placed with a note, vector is sharp at any size.
The proof shows it in its spot and the print file draws it at print resolution; the check runs again when the order is placed.
Client emailed their logo? On the print job, The client's artwork → Add or Replace artwork puts it in the box, checked the same way, and re-renders the job.

entries.title: Choose exactly what each client API key may do — and change it any time
items: Customer → Client portal → API keys: Place orders now has boxes for what an order may carry — ship to any address, choose carrier and service, rush, a ship date, personalized products. A key sending something it isn't allowed gets a clear refusal naming the box.
New: Cancel orders — a key may cancel an order before the warehouse starts on it.
Change permissions on any existing key, right in the Keys list. Keys issued before keep everything they could already do.

entries.title: Change SKU codes when a brand renumbers — stock stays put, old codes keep working
items: A live SKU's code can now change: its page → SKU code → Change…. It stays the same SKU, so stock, locations, lots and history don't move and nothing is transferred.
A whole brand at once: Customer → SKUs → Change SKU codes — paste or upload old and new codes, check every row, then change them all together. Undo puts the old codes back.

The old code keeps working everywhere: old placards and case labels scan, and packing lists, sheets, orders, inbound, the client API, the ordering platform and Shopify that still say it find the SKU. Pick and pack show “was …” for 60 days.

entries.title: The print designer stops adding fields by accident
items: Clicking a dotted line of the customer's PDF now only picks it; Make it a field (or a double-click, or Enter) turns it into a field. Clicking around the page to select or deselect never adds anything.
Your fields sit on top of the PDF's dotted lines, so clicking a field always selects it — and a line a field already covers stops showing.
Leaving the designer with unsaved changes asks first.

entries.title: The design studio saves your work as you go
items: Every change in the portal design studio is kept as your draft within a moment — the top bar shows Draft saved with the time. Close the tab and the studio reopens on your changes next time, with Start from live instead if you'd rather not.
Buyers still see only what you Publish; a half-finished design never goes live on its own.

entries.title: Move a portal design from test to live with one file
items: Design studio → Design file downloads the whole look as one file — pictures, logo and web fonts included — and brings one in on another portal or install, as unpublished changes to check before Publish.
Featured products match by SKU code and user groups by name; anything the other portal doesn't have is listed after the import.
Also on the API: GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/portal-theme/export and POST …/portal-theme/import.

entries.title: Sub-categories as big blocks, and category pictures that fit
items: A parent category shows its sub-categories as big picture blocks, the same as Shop by category on the home page — including a parent with nothing in it yet. Design studio → Catalog switches between blocks (the default), chips, or only the sidebar and menu.
Category pictures always show whole — a logo is fitted inside its block, never cropped.
